items.title: mcpx: portable procStat for darwin via sysctl kern.proc (#7063)
items.body: Fixes #7063. `procStat` in `internal/mcpclient` read `/proc//stat` unconditionally, so process start-time identity (used by stdio handoff detach/adopt to tell a recycled pid from the original child) had no implementation on darwin, breaking the handoff tests and the darwin package build there (dezren39/nix#471 evidence via #237). ## Change - `handoff.go`: the `/proc` implementation moves out; `ProcessStartTime`/`childAlive` keep calling the per-platform `procStat`. Start-time units are documented as platform-defined — a value is only compared for equality on the same machine. - `procstat_linux.go`: the existing `/proc//stat` reader, unchanged. - `procstat_darwin.go`: reads the kernel record via `sysctl kern.proc.pid` (`golang.org/x/sys/unix`, already a module dependency): start time = `p_starttime` in microseconds since the epoch; zombie = `p_stat == SZOMB` (5, spelled out — x/sys/unix does not export it for darwin). - `procstat_other.go` (`!linux && !darwin`): explicit "unavailable on this platform" error instead of a doomed `/proc` read. - `procstat_test.go`: `TestProcStatSelf` — oracle is the kernel's record of the test process itself (exists, non-zero, stable across calls, not a zombie; a negative pid errors). ## Verification - `go test ./internal/mcpclient/ ./internal/pool/ -count=1` on Linux (laptop): PASS (includes the handoff suites and the new `TestProcStatSelf`). - `pkgs/mcpx/scripts/darwin-compile-check.sh`: PASS — darwin/arm64 build of the whole module plus every package's test compile, 0 exceptions. Cross-repo remainder (per #7063 acceptance): advance the mcpx pin in dezren39/nix so dezren39/nix#471's parked aarch64-darwin verification can resume — that step belongs to the nix repo and is named here as the follow-on, not done in this PR. Queue: task 12056 (repo-health-code-pilot), lane code-f. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Process handoff now reads process start times on Linux and macOS, helping distinguish a running process from another process that later reuses its ID. * **Bug Fixes** * On other platforms, handoff now reports an explicit error when process start-time identification is unavailable.
